a2_vs_a1_milk: Read the carton for a Jersey or Guernsey herd, or the A2 seal.
air_chilled_chicken: Check the package for “retained water up to”. That percentage is water.
almond_milk: Read the Nutrition Facts for added sugars, then the protein.
bacon: Find the asterisk beside “no nitrates added” and read the curing ingredients.
bagels: Ask the baker about a water bath before the dough reaches the oven.
baking_soda_powder: Check the date, then test opened powder in hot water for foam.
baking_soda_soak: Soak the fruit twelve minutes, then rinse it clean.
bean_soak_salt: Stir a heaped tablespoon of salt into the soaking water.
beans_dried_vs_canned: Fill a bag from the bulk bin. Whole beans, no split skins.
beef_cuts_basics: Look for fine white flecks through the muscle, not a thick fat rim.
beef_grades_usda: Buy Select for the braise and put the money into Choice steaks.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed: Look for a whole-life seal: American Grassfed, or Certified Grassfed by AGW.
berries_picking: Flip the container and check for juice stains or fuzz.
bison: Find the triangle inspection seal or a state mark on the package.
bottled_water_buying: Turn the bottle over and find the town and state it came from.
bread_aisle: Read the first ingredient for “whole”, then check which stamp is shown.
breakfast_cereal: Compare the added-sugars line and check which Whole Grain Stamp is shown.
broth: Read the Nutrition Facts for sodium, which varies from carton to carton.
bulk_bins_buying: Choose the full, busy bins over a dusty half-empty one.
buns_rolls: Read the name on the bag for “whole wheat”, not “wheat” or “enriched”.
butcher_counter_asking: Ask for the bones and trim behind the counter, usually free.
canned_coconut_milk: Read the ingredients for gums such as guar gum.
canned_fish_choosing: Read the pack medium: “vegetable oil” means a seed-oil blend.
canned_soup: Read the front for “low sodium” versus “reduced sodium”; they differ.
canned_tuna: Find “light” or a skipjack species name, then read the packing ingredients.
cheese_real_vs_processed: Read the bag for potato starch, cellulose and natamycin before buying shreds.
chicken_breast: Read the front for any added liquid percentage, then check the ingredients.
chicken_cuts_basics: Take the pack with the skin still on. It bastes itself.
clams_mussels_oysters: Ask to see the shellfish tag, then tap any open shell.
cocoa: Read the label for “processed with alkali” after the name.
coconut_milk_beverage: Read the carton for “beverage” in the name, then the thickeners.
coconut_water: Check the carton for a “Contains __ percent juice” line.
coffee_beans: Check the bag’s seal and keep the coffee closed between uses.
condiments: Check the serving size, a spoonful, before comparing two jars.
cooking_oils: Read the label for which oil is in the bottle, then its processing.
cottage_cheese: Check beside the name for “directly set”. That wording means acid set the curd.
crab: Check that live crabs move their legs before one is bagged.
crackers: Read the front for “multigrain”; it does not mean whole grain.
cream_cheese: Read the ingredients for a culture, then count the stabilizers after it.
cream_vs_creamer: Read the panel for milkfat percent — real cream states 36% or 10.5%.
cured_pork: Find the asterisk beside “uncured” and read what it points to.
dairy_case: Read the side panel for added vitamins, then any grazing or filtering claim.
deli: Check the cold case first; meats, cheeses and salads all need it.
deli_meat_uncured: Ask the counter to slice whole roasted meat thin instead.
deli_salads: Check the date; keep it at the back of the fridge, not the door.
dried_fruit: Read the ingredients for sulfites or sugar added to the fruit.
dried_herbs: Check the label for the irradiation logo and “treated with radiation”.
dry_brine: Weigh out salt at one percent of the meat’s weight.
duck_meat: Read the class on the label, then look for the Grade A shield.
egg_duck_quail: Check that each shell is clean and uncracked before the carton goes in.
egg_feed_claims: Check whether the carton claims outdoor access and no animal protein at once.
egg_freshness: Find the three-digit number beside the plant code. Higher is fresher.
egg_grades_sizes: Read the weight per dozen on the carton end: 24, 27, 30 ounces.
egg_labels: Check the small regional cartons. That is where a feed claim appears.
egg_shell_color: Read the feed words printed on the carton. Skip the yolk photo.
egg_storage: Move the eggs off the fridge door. It swings warm every open.
farmed_fish_by_species: Buy the farmed mussels, clams and oysters. They are fed nothing.
fermented: Check the label for “raw” or “unpasteurized”, then the list for vinegar.
fermented_pickles: Read the ingredients for vinegar; none listed means a fermented pickle.
fish_freshness_at_counter: Check it is bedded in ice, not sitting in its own liquid.
flour_basics: Take the smallest whole-wheat bag on the shelf. The germ oil turns.
freezing_produce: Blanch vegetables sixty seconds, chill them, then freeze flat.
fresh_pasta: Check the date, and use an opened pack within 2 to 3 days.
fresh_vs_previously_frozen_fish: Ask the counter “was this previously frozen?” before paying the fresh premium.
frozen_vs_fresh_produce: Read the bag’s ingredient list for one word: the vegetable.
ghee: Read the ingredient list for butter or cream as the only entry.
gluten_free_bread: Find the claim on the bag, then read the ingredient list and the gum.
goat_sheep_dairy: Read the ingredients for which animal’s milk went in.
grains_beyond_rice: Grab bulgur or quinoa for a weeknight — both cook in fifteen minutes.
grassfed_butter: Pick the deepest yellow block through the wrapper window. Grass-fed runs near orange.
ground_beef_lean_ratio: Read the cut name too: “ground chuck” beats plain “ground beef.”
ground_beef_organ_blend: Read the ingredient list for liver and heart, each with a percentage.
ground_turkey: Read the ingredient list and the fat statement beside any percent-lean claim.
ham: Read the product name for “Water Added” or “Ham and Water Product”.
honey_adulteration: Buy honey with a producer and a region named on the jar.
hot_dogs: Read the meat ingredients and check for “with byproducts” beside the product name.
hot_soy_sauce: Read the ingredients for wheat, and the front for “gluten-free”.
hummus: Read the ingredients for guar gum, which keeps the dip from weeping.
ice_cream: Read the small print under the flavor for “frozen dairy dessert”.
jam: Read the label for “reduced sugar”, then keep the opened jar cold.
judging_meat_at_the_case: Check the package is sealed and not leaking juices, then smell it.
ketchup_mustard: Check the jar for an open date, or write one on it at home.
kimchi: Check the packed date, then read the list for fish sauce or shrimp.
kombucha: Read the Nutrition Facts for added sugars, then any alcohol statement.
label_artificial_color: Check candy, frosting and white dressings for “color added” near the list’s end.
label_cage_free: Read the carton for a welfare certifier: Certified Humane, AWA, G.A.P.
label_cold_pressed_expeller: Read the oil name first, then look for a process word.
label_front_vs_back: Read three things: ingredient list, added sugars, serving size.
label_grass_fed_term: Look for “100%” or “grass-finished” printed on the package.
label_ingredient_order: Stop reading at “contains 2% or less” — the rest is a trace.
label_lightly_sweetened: Scan the ingredient list for syrup, cane juice, and concentrate.
label_made_with_real: Count how far down it sits. Past third is a trace.
label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain: Read the first ingredient — it must say “whole wheat flour.”
label_natural: Look for a defined word instead: organic, grass-finished, or pasture-raised.
label_no_added_hormones: Look for a third-party verifier on the beef and dairy claim.
label_no_artificial_flavors: Look for “natural flavors” further down the list — the claim leaves it in.
label_nonGMO_vs_organic: Buy the USDA Organic seal alone — paying for both is paying twice.
label_organic_scope: Flip the organic box over. The seal says nothing about the ingredients.
label_pasture_raised_feed: Read both sides of the carton — space and feed are separate claims.
label_serving_size: Check both packages list the same serving size before comparing anything.
label_sugar_free_substitutes: Read the list for erythritol, maltitol, stevia, sucralose — one is there.
label_third_party_seals: Trace the seal to an organization, not the brand’s own logo.
label_wild_vs_farm_raised: Buy the skin-on fillet. A bare one is the easy one to substitute.
lamb_goat: Look for a USDA grade on lamb, and press goat for firm flesh.
lard_tallow: Read the label for “hydrogenated lard” or “lard stearin”.
lobster: Ask the counter to lift the lobster and check the tail curls under.
maple_syrup: Read the front for the standard name, not table or pancake syrup.
mayo: Read the ingredients for which oil comes first, whatever the front says.
meat_case: Read the primal cut on the label, such as chuck or round.
mercury_by_fish: Check the species name on the case tag. Size predicts the mercury.
milk_processing: Read the carton for “ultra-pasteurized”. A date months out gives it away.
miso: Read the ingredients for which grain went in with the soybeans.
muesli: Read the ingredients for sugar, honey or syrup beyond the dried fruit.
natto: Check the date on the pack, since chilled natto keeps only days.
no_antibiotics_poultry: Look for “USDA Process Verified” beside the claim, or put it back.
nut_butter_ingredients: Check the reduced-fat jar’s list — the fat came out and sugar went in.
nutritional_yeast: Read the ingredients for added vitamins, which mark a fortified yeast.
nuts_raw_vs_roasted: Read the ingredient line for cottonseed or soybean oil before buying roasted.
oat_milk: Compare the protein line and read the ingredients for added vitamins and minerals.
oats_steelcut_rolled_instant: Turn the canister over. One ingredient, and it is oats.
olive_oil_grades: Read “product of”, not “packed in” — they name different countries.
olives: Check the jar date, and finish an opened jar within 2 weeks.
organ_meats: Check the use-by date against the night it will be cooked.
organic_worth_it_by_type: Spend the organic money on berries, greens, and apples.
pasta_dry: Turn the box over and read the flour and any added ingredients.
pasta_sauce: Read the ingredients for anything listed ahead of the tomatoes.
pastries_muffins: Read the fat in the ingredients, or ask the baker if it is butter.
plain_kefir: Read the ingredient list for milk and kefir cultures only.
plant_butter: Read the ingredient list and find which oil comes first.
popcorn: Read the ingredients for anything listed besides popcorn.
pork_cuts_and_enhanced: Read the fine print for “contains up to”. Brine is sold by weight.
potato_chips: Read the label for “made from dried potatoes”, the mark of a pressed chip.
precut_produce_tradeoffs: Check the use-by date, since pre-cut spoils days before whole produce does.
prepared_meals: Check the case thermometer, and pans filled no higher than the rim.
pretzel_bread: Ask the baker whether the dough gets a lye or baking-soda bath.
pretzels: Check for a deep brown, glossy crust; the alkaline bath gives it.
produce_apples_pears: Turn each apple or pear over and leave any bruised or damaged one behind.
produce_brassicas: Check for closed, dark green florets, then press the head for soft spots.
produce_citrus: Choose citrus that feels firm with unblemished rind, and leave the soft ones.
produce_green_beans: Check the pods and leave any that are flabby, rust-spotted or sticky.
produce_leafy_greens: Check the leaves stand crisp and fully green, then keep them cold at home.
produce_mushrooms: Check each cap and leave any that feels damp or soft.
produce_onions_garlic: Squeeze the bulb, smell it, and keep it out of the plastic bag.
produce_peppers: Pick a firm, unbruised pepper and pass on any that has shriveled or softened.
produce_picking_ripeness: Ignore the country line and check the item for give and weight.
produce_ripeness_by_item: Smell the stem end on anything that ripens after picking.
produce_root_vegetables: Press each root for firmness, and twist the tops off carrots before storing.
produce_seasonality: Read the farmers’ market as the signal for what is in season locally.
produce_stone_fruit: Look the fruit over for bruises or damage and skip any that shows one.
produce_storage: Keep apples and bananas out of the drawer with your greens and berries.
rancidity_check: Smell for old paint or crayons. That one is finished.
raw_aged_cheese: Read the rind label for an age in months.
raw_cider_vinegar: Read the label for “diluted” or a second vinegar named in a blend.
raw_kefir: Buy it from the refrigerated case, never the shelf-stable carton.
raw_milk: Buy from a farm you can visit that posts its test results.
revive_greens: Trim the stem ends and stand them in ice water thirty minutes.
rice_arsenic: Read the origin on the bag: India, Pakistan or California.
rotisserie_chicken: Read the ingredient list: two words is plain; water second means a solution.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed: Take the frozen sockeye from the freezer case, not the fresh Atlantic.
salsa: Read the ingredients for the acid: vinegar, lime or lemon juice.
salt: Read the label for “does not supply iodide” beside the salt’s name.
sandwich_bread: Read the flour names; “wheat” and “enriched” alone do not establish whole grain.
sauerkraut: Read the ingredients for cabbage and salt only, with no vinegar listed.
scallops: Read the ingredients for a phosphate and water, or ask if they are dry.
seafood_certifications: Check the badge names a program you can look up. Unnamed is marketing.
seafood_counter: Ask the counter for the species name, then check the fish sits on ice.
seaweed: Read the package for the seaweed’s kind by name, not just “seaweed”.
seeds: Check the bag date, and keep opened flax cold once home.
shrimp_imported_vs_domestic: Read the country-of-origin line on the bag, then look for BAP or ASC.
smoked_salmon: Read the label for nova, lox or kippered, then keep it refrigerated.
snack_bars: Read the ingredients for high fructose corn syrup and hydrogenated oils.
snacks: Check veggie chips for potato flour colored with vegetable powder.
sour_cream: Read the name on the tub for “cultured” or “acidified”.
sourdough: Ask the baker what leavens the dough; check for culture or starter.
soy_milk: Find calcium and vitamin D on the panel, and check for added sugars.
specialty_flours: Read the flour name for “whole”, then check the fat line.
sprouted_grain_bread: Read the first few ingredients, then check the rest for added flour.
sprouted_grains: Check the label names the grain as whole, not only its process.
sprouts_raw: Check the roots are still white and the clamshell is not fogged.
strawberries_organic_residue: Check the clamshell for the USDA Organic seal before it goes in.
sugars: Read the ingredients for cane or beet; both make the same sugar.
tea: Read the box for “decaffeinated”, since true tea holds caffeine otherwise.
tempeh: Read the ingredients for soybeans alone or added grains, and check for mold.
tortilla_chips: Read the ingredients for masa; plain cornmeal makes a corn chip instead.
tortillas: Check for masa or masa harina, then read for added wheat and fat.
trail_mix: Read the ingredients for anything added beyond the nuts and fruit.
turkey_bacon: Read the small print under the name for the meat cuts used.
turkey_whole: Check the product name for “basted”, “self-basted”, or an added-solution statement.
venison_game: Ask whether each animal was handled separately and kept cold throughout.
vinegar: Read the label for “unpasteurized”; most vinegar is pasteurized otherwise.
washing_produce: Scrub the firm ones with a brush. Rinse and spin the greens.
white_fish: Ask which species it is, then press the flesh for spring-back.
whole_spices: Toast them in a dry pan until they smell, then grind.
whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk: Read the milkfat percentage on the panel, not the cap color.
yogurt_live_cultures: Find “live and active cultures” on the tub. Shelf-stable never carries it.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored: Take the big plain tub, not the single-serve fruit cups.
